chunks: Al-Kafi: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all together, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A man -if he used to know a chapter and then forgets it or abandons it and then enters paradise- she appears to him from above in a most beautiful form and says: 'Do you know me?' He says: 'No' She says: 'I am such and such chapter, you did not act by me and abandoned me, by Allah if you had acted by me I would have made you reach this station,' and she points with her hand above her

key_terms.تَعْمَلْ بِي: To act by me (implementing the teachings)

ai.seo_question: What happens to a Surah if a person forgets or neglects it?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the personification of Quranic chapters as intercessors in Paradise, highlighting the tangible spiritual cost of neglecting their practice. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on 'Amal bi-l-Qur'an' (acting upon the Quran), where mere memorization is insufficient without implementation, as the Surah itself testifies to the believer's level of devotion. The imagery of the Surah pointing upwards signifies that adherence to its specific teachings could have elevated the believer to even greater ranks of proximity to Allah.
